messages.content: What wheather is now in Moscow, in celsius?

function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time weather data. You can check a reliable weather website or app (e.g., the Weather Channel, AccuWeather, or a local Russian service) for the current temperature in Moscow.

We don't have real-time data. We can approximate or say we don't have real-time data. But we can use a weather API? We don't have direct API. We can respond that we don't have real-time data. Or we can approximate based on typical weather. But better to say we don't have real-time data. The user might want a real-time answer. We can say we can't fetch real-time data. Alternatively, we could use a placeholder. But we should not fabricate. So we should respond that we don't have real-time data.
